versions.changelog: Kept from round 1; writePrivate now opens O_CREAT|O_EXCL first to know whether it created the file; §3, the manifest paragraph, the expiry bullet and the export; The card now describes the relay (confirmed:true throws with destination and scope, index-only default, no ove; Every claim is now scoped to the path that does it; Added node to requires; _meta; Staged /tmp/clawscan-fix/stage/chatgpt-exporter
Force 0700/0600 on reused paths; redact summary.md; remove allowUnsafeDest; browser-relay only, no bearer token.
Purge deletes only the exact export dir; token never written to disk.

Fixes an unconstrained delete and a silently-dropped permissions block. --purge now validates its target: absolute path under $HOME, at least two levels deep, not a symlink, must contain an index.json this tool produced; it refuses $HOME, / and anything outside your home, and refuses to run non-interactively. Previously a stray -o path could point the delete at a parent directory. The frontmatter also had TWO openclaw keys, so YAML kept the last one and the entire declared-permissions block was discarded at parse time — merged, and the delete capability is now declared explicitly.

Documents the --purge command that 1.7.0 shipped without describing. A destructive command that is not in the documentation is exactly the doc/behaviour mismatch this skill was being flagged for, and adding one while fixing others was my error. --purge deletes the local export tree, prints the path and size first, requires a typed PURGE confirmation, refuses non-interactively, and never touches your ChatGPT account.

Adds the cleanup half of an export tool. --purge deletes the local exports, shows their size first and requires a typed PURGE confirmation, refusing non-interactively. An export is a plaintext copy of every conversation you have had, so leaving it on disk indefinitely was the larger risk; there is now a documented off-switch. Index-only remains the default and full content still requires --full plus an interactive confirmation.
Bearer token is written to a 0600 header file and passed to curl with -H @file, never as an argv secret. Index-only remains the TypeScript default.
Index-only is now the real TypeScript default; conversation IDs are validated before interpolation; unpinned npx tsx shebang removed so install cannot pull unreviewed remote code.

Closes the consent bypass and inverts the risky default. Index-only is now the DEFAULT; exporting full message text requires --full AND an interactive typed confirmation, and --yes can no longer wave it through non-interactively (previously a scripted caller could dump every conversation silently). The hidden TTY prompt is now the preferred token path, with the environment variable demoted to a warned fallback. Adds a machine-readable permissions block.

Security and disclosure pass. Adds a Permissions, Data Flow & Consent section declaring every capability, what data is touched, where it is written and what leaves the machine. Documents the off-switch and requires explicit opt-in for privacy-affecting or destructive actions. Removes documentation claims the shipped code did not implement. No functionality removed.
